findings.title: No refuge becomes concrete failure
findings.claim: Within the pericope, 18:43 turns the earlier absence of any refuge apart from God into two concrete failures: no faction comes to his aid, and he cannot vindicate himself.
findings.mechanism: The exclusion boundary in 18:27 is repeated in the focus, while the focus's collective-help and self-vindication forms divide unavailable refuge into social and reflexive rescue.
findings.reader_payoff: The owner's isolation becomes the enacted form of the passage's earlier refuge claim, rather than a merely contingent lack of nearby supporters.
findings.containment: The ordinary statement that no faction helped him and that he did not save himself remains intact. The deliberate reprise is an attributed contextual inference; 18:27 is not treated as having only this function.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic anchors and coordinates are supplied, but the nomination is legacy_unbound and the refuge branch has no independent lexicon record in the packet.

findings.title: The possession ledger reverses

findings.mechanism: The earlier existence-plus-possession construction and the boast of wealth and followers are answered by negated existence in the focus; the focus's faction and aid forms expose the failure of accumulated assets to become operative support.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus reads as the balancing line of the garden owner's boast, where having resources and having effective help are no longer interchangeable.
findings.containment: The finding does not deny the narrative contrast between earlier abundance and later loss. The ledger is an attributed macro relation, not a claim that the focus's ordinary grammar is itself a financial metaphor.

epistemic.reason: The mirrored anchors and focus returns are supplied, while the formal ledger relation remains a legacy_unbound contextual inference.
